newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Namibia lifts some forex controls.
newsitem.headline: Namibia lifts some forex controls.

text.p: The central Bank of Nambia has lifted some foreign exchange controls on offshore investments, capital and current account transactions and travel allowances.

The bank said in a statement issued on Tuesday that the move was in line with the Southern African Development Community (SADC)'s initiative towards the free flow of goods, services and people across the 12-member countries' borders.
Under the new regulations, the limit for direct foreign investment has been increased from N$20 million to N$40 million.

"Nambian corporates will now be allowed to raise financing abroad on the strength of their local balance sheet, while in the past offshore financing had to be obtained without any recourse to or guarantee from Namibia," the statement said.

During 1997, institutional investors will be permitted offshore investment of up to three percent of the net inflow of funds for 1996, subject to the overall limit of 10 percent of the total assets of the institutional investor.
Institutions may also request the bank to allow curreny transfers of up to two percent of the net inflow of funds during 1996 -- to be listed on registered stock exchanges in any SADC country.
The bank said the annual travel allowance for Namibian citizens has been increased from N$60,000 to N$80,000 per person. Children under 12 will be allowed a maximum of N$25,000.

SADC, which groups Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe, represents 40 percent of Africa's population and 80 percent of the continent's GDP.
